svg.title: Tension components for the tightrope walker
svg.desc: Left: the tension TL in the left part of the wire points 5.0° above the −x direction and has components TLx (left) and TLy (up); the tension TR points 5.0° above the +x direction and has components TRx (right) and TRy (up). Right: the free-body diagram of the walker with TLx left, TRx right, TLy and TRy up and the weight W down; the net force in x and in y is zero. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Less sag means much more tension
T = w / (2 sin θ): the two vertical components must still add to w. At 5.0°, a 70.0-kg walker needs
3.94 kN in each half of the wire.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
